Training set attacks (A01–A06) — what your model has seen:
A01 — NN-based TTS (SPSS). Flite front-end → HMM duration → AR RNN acoustic model with VAE speaker embedding → WaveNet vocoder. This is the high-quality neural vocoder system.
A02 — Same architecture as A01 (same front-end, same acoustic model, same VAE) except it uses the WORLD vocoder instead of WaveNet. WORLD is a signal-processing vocoder (source-filter model), not neural. A01 and A02 are explicitly designed as a minimal pair: same everything except waveform generator.
A03 — NN-based TTS using the Merlin toolkit with Festival front-end. Feedforward acoustic model (not RNN), one-hot speaker embedding. Also uses the WORLD vocoder. So A02 and A03 share the vocoder but differ in acoustic model architecture.
A04 — Waveform concatenation TTS (unit selection). CART-based duration/F0 prediction, diphone unit selection with target/join costs. No neural vocoder at all — this splices actual recorded speech segments together. This is the "legacy" system, same algorithm as ASVspoof 2015's hardest attack (S10). A16 in the eval set uses the identical algorithm.
A05 — NN-based voice conversion (not TTS). Uses a VAE as the conversion model with WORLD vocoder. Takes human speech as input and converts speaker identity. Doesn't need parallel training data. A17 in eval uses the same VAE framework but swaps WORLD for direct waveform modification.
A06 — Transfer-function-based voice conversion. GMM-UBM alignment, LPC spectral filtering + overlap-add. Completely non-neural — this is classical signal processing VC. A19 in eval uses the same algorithm.
So the families in your training set are:
The WORLD vocoder family is A02, A03, and A05. Three systems all using the same signal-processing vocoder, differing in what feeds into it (two TTS acoustic models vs one VC model). This is your largest shared-component cluster.
A01 stands alone as the only WaveNet-based system in training. It's architecturally paired with A02 (same everything except vocoder), which makes A01 vs A02 comparison extremely informative — any difference in your attention patterns between them is caused by the WaveNet vs WORLD distinction.
A04 stands alone as waveform concatenation. Non-parametric synthesis, no vocoder at all.
A06 stands alone as classical signal-processing VC.
Eval set attacks (A07–A19) — unseen by your model:
Briefly: A07 uses WORLD vocoder with GAN post-filtering. A08 uses a neural source-filter waveform model. A09 uses the Vocaine vocoder. A10 is Tacotron 2 end-to-end TTS with a WaveRNN vocoder and speaker verification transfer learning. A11 is identical to A10 except using Griffin-Lim instead of WaveRNN. A12 uses autoregressive WaveNet. A13 is a combined VC+TTS system with waveform filtering. A14 is a combined VC+TTS system using the STRAIGHT vocoder. A15 is the same as A14 but with speaker-dependent WaveNet vocoders. A16 uses the same waveform concatenation as A04. A17 uses the same VAE framework as A05 but with direct waveform modification instead of WORLD. A18 is i-vector/PLDA VC with a DNN glottal vocoder. A19 uses the same algorithm as A06. arXiv
The clustering from the original paper's dendrogram confirms: the closest pairs are A10/A11, A14/A15, and A01/A02, which share the same TTS architecture but differ in waveform generation. The VC systems using human speech as source (A05, A06, A17, A18, A19) cluster together on one branch
